children.text: Sarrat Church is the Santa Monica Parish Church in the town of Sarrat, about 8 km southeast of Laoag, and is counted as the largest church in Ilocos Norte. The red-brick building was completed in 1779, but earthquake damage in 2024 means restoration work is planned, so always check whether it is open before you visit.
The official name is Santa Monica Parish Church, but locals simply call it Sarrat Church. It stands in the poblacion of Sarrat, about
8 km
southeast of Laoag City, the provincial capital of Ilocos Norte. According to Wikipedia, the red-brick building is about
long, about
wide and about
high, which makes it the largest church in Ilocos Norte and one with one of the longest naves in the country. Its style mixes the Philippine "Earthquake Baroque" with Neoclassical elements.

The history goes back to the arrival of Spanish Augustinian missionaries. Sarrat was originally a visita (a small community without its own church) of Laoag, and it was first named after Saint Michael (San Miguel) because the first Augustinian missionaries arrived on September 29, 1724, the feast of Saint Michael. The parish of Santa Monica was established that same year in 1724, a convent was built in 1769 to serve as a temporary chapel, and the church, the belfry, the convent and the elevated brick stairway (curillo) connecting them were all completed in 1779. The church was destroyed on March 3, 1816, rebuilt in 1848, and damaged by fire in 1882, so it has been repaired many times.

Sarrat also has a place in the history of Ilocos Norte. According to a Manila Bulletin report, the church stands on the second town site, called "San Miguel de Cuncunig," after the first town site was destroyed by a great fire during the 1815 Sarrat Revolt. When Ilocos Norte became an official province in 1818, San Miguel de Cuncunig is said to have become its first capital. In modern times the church has strong ties with the Marcos family: Imelda Marcos led a restoration in June 1977, and in June 1983 Irene, the daughter of President Ferdinand Marcos, was married here. Sarrat is also the birthplace of former president Ferdinand Marcos.

There is something travelers must know. Several strong earthquakes in 2024 (February, June and December) badly damaged the structure, and church authorities were reported to have vacated the building in early 2025. In June 2025 the Diocese of Laoag and the National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP) signed a restoration agreement, and about

was set aside for the first phase, covering repairs to the roof and wooden trusses and reinforcement of the brick walls. Work was expected to begin in September 2025, but I could not confirm progress since then at the time of writing. For that reason this guide treats the visit as a half-day trip to see the exterior and feel the town's history rather than to go inside the church. Check with the Diocese of Laoag or the Ilocos Norte tourism office before you go.
A building about

long looks very different from far away and up close. The broad brick walls and thick buttresses are typical of a Philippine Baroque church. In earthquake-prone areas, the style of building with thick walls to protect the structure is called "Earthquake Baroque."

A bell tower with a clock stands beside the church and strikes every half hour. The tower collapsed in a magnitude 5.3 earthquake on August 17, 1983 and was later restored. The convent was called "Casa del Palacio Real" (House of the Royal Palace) and at various times served as the municipal hall and housed the Colegio de Santa Monica.

blocks.title: The curillo linking church and convent

children.text: The church and convent are linked by a three-level brick stairway (the curillo, or bridge staircase). It is an unusual structure connecting the two buildings and a good spot for photos. Because it is a part that suffered earthquake damage, access may be restricted.

The ground floor of the convent has housed a parish museum and photo gallery since 1994. It is a small space with church artifacts and old photographs, but I could not confirm whether it is open since the building was damaged. If a door is open, ask at the parish office.
Fourteen brick Stations of the Cross (sculptures showing the 14 scenes of Jesus's path to the cross) surround the church. You can walk around the outside and slowly look at the brickwork and crosses.
The National Museum of the Philippines declared the church an Important Cultural Property on September 27, 2009. Restoration was reported to be led by the NHCP.
The church was used as a stand-in for the parish church of Arayat, Pampanga, in the 2015 film "Heneral Luna." Film fans can enjoy imagining the scenes in the churchyard.

blocks.title: Sarrat town and the Marcos birthplace

children.text: The town has a Marcos Museum (in the Edralin House) and the Marcos birthplace. According to the Ilocos Norte tourism office fee list, the Sarrat birthplace costs
for adults, is free for children, senior citizens, students and persons with disabilities, and is listed as open
to
. Other sources describe split morning and afternoon hours, so confirm the hours and fee locally. Because opinion about this figure is divided, we suggest approaching it as a historical exhibit.

items.title: Half day from Laoag
items.subtitle: The church exterior and a stroll around town

children.text: Take a jeepney or tricycle from central Laoag to Sarrat. The jeepney is said to take about
15-20 minutes
one way.
From the square in front of the church, take in the whole building, then walk slowly along the wall that is about
long.
Look at the exterior structures such as the bell tower, convent and curillo, and do not go inside any area with safety signs.
Check in town whether the Marcos birthplace and museum are open, and look around.
Return to Laoag and have lunch with Ilocano food (such as empanada).
During restoration work, screens and closures may hide the church facade. In that case, be content with viewing it from a distance from the town square.

items.title: A full day in Ilocos Norte
items.subtitle: Laoag, Sarrat and Paoay

children.text: Start with Laoag Cathedral and its leaning bell tower.
Move on to Sarrat and look around the church exterior.
Have lunch and a rest in central Laoag.
Go to Paoay Church and see the buttresses of this World Heritage church.
Watch the sunset at the La Paz Sand Dunes and return to Laoag.
Combining several stops in one day makes for long travel times, so look into renting a car or hiring a tricycle for the day.
There are flights from Manila to Laoag International Airport (LAO), and the flight takes about
1 hour
. Airlines and schedules change by season, so check when you book.
From Laoag Airport, take a tricycle or taxi into the city. Sarrat is farther out from the city, so it is easier to change in the city than to go straight from the airport.
Flight routes change often, so check airline announcements before departure.
Buses run from Manila (Cubao in Quezon City, and Pasay) to Laoag, operated by companies such as GV Florida, Partas and Viron Transit. The trip takes about
10–12 hours
, and fares should be checked locally.
According to Wikipedia, the road distance from Manila to Laoag is about
480 km
(via the southern route). Night buses have both sleeper-type and regular seats.
Sarrat is about
8 km
from Laoag. Jeepneys run daily from central Laoag to Sarrat, and the trip takes about
15-20 minutes
one way.
Within the town, use a tricycle. Check the fare locally and agree on it before you ride.

The Laoag area has a tropical savanna climate, with a dry season of roughly November to April and a wet season of roughly May to October (sources differ slightly on the boundary months). The driest months are February and March (about 3–15 mm of rain a month, depending on the source) and the wettest is August (about 520–590 mm), and December to February is generally described as the most comfortable time for walking. Because you will be walking around outdoor architecture, the dry season is more comfortable.
In April and May the daytime high reaches about

and it is hot. Move around early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Church events are held during Holy Week (the week before Easter), but the church may not be open during construction. About four to five typhoons a year are said to pass through, so leave spare days in your rainy-season schedule.

Sarrat has few large places to stay, so most travelers stay in central Laoag and visit as a half-day trip. Laoag has many hotels and guesthouses and is close to the airport. If you plan to tour all of Ilocos Norte, it is easiest to use Laoag as your base.

In Ilocos Norte, people often look for foods such as empanada (a fried rice-dough pastry) and longganisa (Ilocano-style sausage). Restaurant names change often, so check locally for places with good reviews before you go.
Before you go, ask the Diocese of Laoag or the Ilocos Norte tourism office (email tourismilocosnorte@gmail.com, phone +63 77 772 1213) whether the church is open.
If you can go inside, modest clothing that covers shoulders and knees is best. Refrain from taking photos during Mass.
If you travel by jeepney from central Laoag, ask about the last jeepney times for going and coming back.
The midday heat is intense, so bring a hat, water and sunscreen. There is little shade around the church.
For photos, shoot wide from the square in front, and focus on the brick texture on the sides, to show the scale.
The Marcos birthplace and museum have short opening hours, so check them before the church.
Carry plenty of cash (pesos). Many places in small towns do not accept cards.
If you combine Laoag Cathedral and Paoay Church in one trip, you can compare Spanish-era churches in Ilocos Norte.
The 2024 earthquakes badly damaged the church, the building has been vacated since early 2025, and restoration work may be planned or under way. Never cross any barrier tape.
Opening hours, fees and construction status change often. This guide is based on June 2025 news reports and Wikipedia, so check the latest announcements.
The church building has cracks and a risk of falling debris, so do not stand directly beneath the walls for long.
Do not make noise or talk loudly during Mass or funerals.
Watch out for midday heat, rainy-season showers and the typhoon season, and check local weather information.
Opinions about the Marcos family differ widely. When viewing exhibits in town, it is best to avoid political arguments.

15-20 minutes
